newsitem.title: USA: Muni groups seek SEC meeting on yield burning.
newsitem.headline: Muni groups seek SEC meeting on yield burning.

text.p: Seven municipal groups asked to meet with Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Arthur Levitt to discuss the commission's "activities" regarding yield burning.
Yield burning refers to allegations that bond underwriters overcharge states and localities for U.S. Treasury securities they bought to help them refinance their outstanding bonds.
The Internal Revenue Service has told municipalities that they can avoid having bonds declared taxable by settling any overcharges with the agency.

But muni groups told top Treasury Department brass at a January 27 meeting that bond dealers, not issuers, generally should pay the overcharges and that the SEC's enforcement staff should take the lead on the matter.

Groups included the National Governors' Association, National Conference of State Legislatures, Council of State Governments, National League of Cities, U.S. conference of mayors, National Association of Counties and the International City/County Management Association.
"We are writing ... to request an opportunity to meet with you regarding the Commission's activities regarding 'yield burning,' " groups said in the March 18 letter to Levitt.
SEC's Levitt had no comment on the groups' letter.

The groups told Levitt that they had met with Donald Lubick, Treasury assistant secretary, on the issue recently. They said they told Lubick that it is the SEC's responsibility to regulate dealers' sales practices and to oversee market integrity by enforcing the federal securities laws.

They asked how "we can coordinate federal, state, and local efforts to protect not just the muni market from potential abuse, but also so that we are working with each other and not at cross purposes."

"As the purchasers of securities that may or may not have been appropriately priced and as the issuers of municipal securities that are being questioned with regard to their integrity, we feel it is important to discuss the role the Commission should play in clearing up the now rampant rumors and allegations regarding yield burning," the groups said.
They said they are the "victims of bad publicity" and may be victims of IRS enforcement actions, "all without the knowledge to respond to the allegations and criticisms."
